Aditya — thanks for the heads up. Summary from Finance review:

- Classification: Blue Horizon is an EU-registered company (non-US entity). We will NOT issue a 1099 for amounts paid to a foreign corporate entity. 1099 reporting only applies to US persons/entities.
- Required doc: W-8BEN-E is the appropriate form for them to certify foreign status and claim any treaty benefits if applicable. Please request a signed W-8BEN-E with their legal name and GIIN if they are an FFI, or at minimum a completed Part I and Part IV where applicable.
- Withholding: No US withholding is required if they provide a valid W-8BEN-E. If they fail to provide it, backup withholding could apply — but this is rare for corporations; finance will place a hold until we have the doc.
- VAT: Our standard approach is to rely on their VAT registration for B2B reverse charge. We need their EU VAT ID on the invoice/PO. If not present, tax team may ask for a self-billing note.
- Payment rail: Their stub indicates SEPA/IBAN. For high-value transfers we prefer SWIFT to avoid currency routing issues; finance can send either but needs confirmation of beneficiary name vs legal entity.

Action items for Aditya: please ask Marta to: 1) attach a signed W-8BEN-E (pdf), 2) confirm legal entity name + VAT ID to appear on invoice, 3) confirm whether they'd prefer SEPA or SWIFT and provide beneficiary legal name exactly as on bank account.
